description: NaCr₂In(H₂O₅)₂ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/m space group. Na is bonded to six O atoms to form NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six equivalent CrO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent InO₆ octahedra. There are four shorter (2.62 Å) and two longer (2.74 Å) Na-O bond lengths. Cr is bonded to four O atoms to form CrO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent InO₆ octahedra and corners with three equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 42-69°. There are a spread of Cr-O bond distances ranging from 1.63-1.71 Å. In is bonded to six O atoms to form InO₆ octahedra that share corners with four equivalent CrO₄ tetrahedra and edges with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. There are four shorter (2.15 Å) and two longer (2.17 Å) In-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to two O atoms. There is one shorter (1.00 Å) and one longer (1.70 Å) H-O bond length. In the second H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one O atom. The H-O bond length is 0.99 Å. There are four inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one In and two H atoms. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted single-bond geometry to one Na and one Cr atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to one Cr and one H atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Cr, and one In atom.
